recognize_zh: 低倍血液抹片中紅血球呈團塊狀，其間散布數顆比淋巴球大的單核細胞，核圓、細胞質中等量淡灰藍色，左下一顆細胞質有泡沫狀空泡，暗示為組織球（histiocyte）；但此倍率下難以確認細節。
features: Scattered large mononuclear cells, clearly larger than adjacent small lymphocytes
Round to oval, eccentric or central nuclei with fine chromatin
Moderate pale gray-blue cytoplasm; one cell at lower left with foamy/vacuolated cytoplasm
Small dark lymphocytes interspersed for size comparison
Red cells aggregated into irregular clumps (thick area or preparation artifact)
describe_en: Low-power view of a peripheral blood smear (thick area, with red cells aggregated into irregular clumps) shows several large mononuclear cells with round to oval nuclei and moderate amounts of pale gray-blue cytoplasm, one of which contains foamy cytoplasmic vacuoles. Small lymphocytes are interspersed and provide a size reference. At this magnification the cells are suggestive of circulating histiocytes/macrophages, but nuclear and cytoplasmic detail is insufficient to exclude monocytes, plasma cells, or other abnormal cells; high-power review (ideally of a buffy coat preparation) is required.

ddx.vs: Monocytes have folded or kidney-shaped nuclei with lacy chromatin and gray cytoplasm with fine azurophilic granules, and are usually smaller than activated histiocytes.
Plasma cells show eccentric nuclei with clock-face chromatin, deep basophilic cytoplasm and a perinuclear hof.
Tumor cells show high N:C ratio, nuclear atypia, prominent nucleoli and often cohesive clusters.
Endothelial cells are elongated with oval nuclei and occur in cohesive sheets from the needle tip rather than as isolated round cells.
